<jats:p>
                    Plasma-based accelerators are beginning to employ relativistic beams with unprecedented charge and ultrashort durations. These dense driver beams can drive wakes even in high-density plasmas (
                    <a:math xmlns:a="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline">
                      <a:mrow>
                        <a:mo>≳</a:mo>
                        <a:msup>
                          <a:mrow>
                            <a:mn>10</a:mn>
                          </a:mrow>
                          <a:mrow>
                            <a:mn>19</a:mn>
                          </a:mrow>
                        </a:msup>
                        <a:mtext> </a:mtext>
                        <a:mtext> </a:mtext>
                        <a:mrow>
                          <a:msup>
                            <a:mrow>
                              <a:mi>cm</a:mi>
                            </a:mrow>
                            <a:mrow>
                              <a:mo>−</a:mo>
                              <a:mn>3</a:mn>
                            </a:mrow>
                          </a:msup>
                        </a:mrow>
                      </a:mrow>
                    </a:math>
                    ), where betatron radiation becomes increasingly important and begins to affect the dynamics of the accelerated beam. We show that betatron cooling leads to a strong structuring of the phase space of the beam. This gives rise to bunched, ring-like structures with positive radial position and momentum gradients, i.e., population inversion of the amplitude of oscillation. We derive the characteristic timescales for this process analytically and confirm our predictions with multidimensional particle-in-cell simulations. The radiation-dominated regime of beam dynamics fundamentally alters the acceleration process and produces self-structured beams; particle-in-cell simulations of the resulting beams show that it becomes unstable to the ion-channel laser and lead to exponential amplification of radiation.
                  </jats:p>
title: Phase-Space Shaping Due to Betatron Cooling in Wakefield Accelerators and the Onset of the Ion-Channel Laser

<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    In plasma science, particle-in-cell/Monte Carlo collision (PIC/MCC) simulations are an important tool. Using them as digital twins for knowledge-based plasma process development requires quantitative agreement with experiments. Based on multiple experimental diagnostics applied to a geometrically symmetric capacitively coupled radio frequency plasma, a 1d3v PIC/MCC code is validated for CF

                    gas. Measurements of the ion flux energy distribution function, electron density, and spatio-temporally resolved F atom excitation rate at a driving frequency of

                    , are compared to simulation results. Ion-neutral cross section data, commonly used in previous work, are found to provide a limited accuracy for the ion dynamics and conversion in the sheaths, resulting in ion flux energy distribution functions at the electrodes that differ significantly from measured data. In agreement with more recent datasets, the ion–neutral cross sections are, therefore, scaled to reproduce the experimental results. The coefficients for ion–ion recombination, secondary electron emission, and electron reflection at the electrodes are systematically varied to achieve precise alignment with the measured plasma properties including the accurate description of electron power absorption mode transitions as a function of the driving voltage amplitude. The choice of the ion–ion recombination coefficient is found to have a strong effect on this mode transition in the simulation. With these key input parameters adjusted, good quantitative agreement between simulation and experimental results is achieved over a wide range of external control parameters providing the basis for quantitatively accurate digital-twin plasma simulations.
                  </jats:p>
